definitions.gloss: abandoned house; dilapidated building; ruined house
definitions.explanation: A house or building that has been abandoned and fallen into disrepair. Often used in the context of rural depopulation or horror settings.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧{廃屋|はいおく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{誰|だれ}も→誰も：18610_daremo⟧⟦{住|す}んでいない→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: Nobody lives in that abandoned house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{村|むら}→村：02261_mura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧はずれ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{廃屋|はいおく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: An old abandoned house remains on the outskirts of the village.

examples.japanese: ⟦{過疎化|かそか}→過疎化：05242_kasoka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}み→進む：01225_susumu⟧、{廃屋|はいおく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{年々|ねんねん}→年々：10417_nennen⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many areas where depopulation is advancing and abandoned houses are increasing year by year.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal word often seen in news articles discussing rural depopulation and urban decay. Also commonly appears in horror and mystery fiction. The issue of {廃屋|はいおく} has become a social problem in Japan due to declining population.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {廃屋|はいおく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}える→増える：01183_fueru⟧ (abandoned houses increase)
- {廃屋|はいおく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{解体|かいたい}→解体：06223_kaitai⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to demolish an abandoned house)
- {廃屋|はいおく}⟦{同然|どうぜん}→同然：09487_douzen⟧ (practically a ruin)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{空|あ}き{家|や}→空き家：03007_akiya⟧: vacant house — may be temporarily unoccupied but not necessarily ruined
- ⟦{廃墟|はいきょ}→廃墟：12453_haikyo⟧: ruins — broader term including any type of ruined structure
